note: The two sets are nearly identical in content, values, units and quotes; both correctly capture the drivetrain properties from the prose and Table 5-1, including the 5% critical damping ratio with its free-free-mode condition and the no-frictional-losses gearbox assumption. The only substantive difference is that Set A states the fully-deployed high-speed shaft brake torque three times (including a third variant 'High-Speed Shaft Brake | Torque | ... | conditions: Fully-Deployed'), whereas Set B states it twice. Both sets duplicate every table fact once under a component name and once under the turbine name, and both omit the DOWEC-derived supporting figures (0.35 MW loss at 6.25 MW aerodynamic power; 5,025,500 kg•m² equivalent low-speed-shaft inertia). Set B is marginally better for less duplication, with no loss of correct content.
remarks: Both sets repeat each Table 5-1 row twice (component-level and 'NREL 5-MW baseline wind turbine'-level claims), a systematic duplication pattern worth suppressing in the extractor. Both also leave out the DOWEC comparison figures (0.35 MW loss at ~6.25 MW aerodynamic power; 5,025,500 kg•m² equivalent low-speed-shaft generator inertia) that justify the 94.4% efficiency and 534.116 kg•m² inertia. Note the prose calls the 0.6 s value a 'time lag' while Table 5-1 labels it 'Time Constant'; both sets follow the table label, which is acceptable but the two names are not reconciled.
